facts.big: If the signal were better, I’d call you
facts.label: Segundo condicional
facts.sub: Use If + passado simples e would + verbo base para situações imaginárias: If I had money, I would buy it. If I were you, I would…

facts.label: se + passado, faria
facts.sub: Use If + passado simples e would + verbo base para situações imaginárias: If I had money, I would travel. If the signal were better, I would call you. O passado depois de if não indica passado real.

facts.label: se eu fosse você
facts.sub: Use If I were you, I would… para dar conselhos: If I were you, I would change my phone company. Se usa were com todas as pessoas, mesmo I, he e she nesta frase.

Peça um exemplo real da vida de cada aluno.

compare.ask: If I were you, I would change.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “se eu tivesse, eu compraria” e “se eu fosse você, eu mudaria”.
compare.tip: Diga: “If I were you, I would change.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use If + passado simples e would + verbo base: If I had money, I would buy a phone. Depois de if não use would. O verbo to be usa were para todas as pessoas: If I were you, If the signal were better. Para conselhos, use If I were you, I would…

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: If I were you, I would change.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: If I had money, I would buy a phone is an imaginary situation.
We say “If I would have money…”.
items.why: We say If I had money…, never if + would.

items.s: We use were after I in If I were you.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: If I had money, I would buy a phone is an imaginary situation. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “If I would have money…”. → Falso (We say If I had money…, never if + would.)
We use were after I in If I were you. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

paragraphs: It is a warm evening in Atlanta. Elsa and Eva sit on a sofa. Elsa looks at her phone again. The signal is very weak. The battery is almost empty. The friends begin to dream a little.

“Eva, I would call you more often if the signal were better here.” says Elsa. “If I were you, I would change my phone company.” says Eva. “If I had more money, I would buy a new phone with a better battery.” says Elsa.
